label: Standard kit, every piece at the shortest gate they all fill, read out of a module's own recordings
audition_title: libsonare drums vs the module's own recordings, the whole kit at one gate
_why: The third of three gates over one source, and the only one that holds the whole kit at once. A kit is not a set of instruments that happen to share a channel - it is a set of relations between its members, and a relation can only be read where every member was measured the same way. Sixty milliseconds is the longest window all twelve families fill, so it is the longest window in which the question `how far do the cymbals sit over the drums` has an answer at all.
_notes: Forty-four of the kit's forty-seven keys. The three that are out record 44, 45 and 49 ms - the maracas, the short guiro and the claves - and nothing here pads a recording to a gate it does not fill. The toms and the cymbals appear here as well as in `drums_module`, deliberately: this grid does not replace that one, it answers a different question at a window too short for the decay that one reads.
_gate: Sixty rather than forty-four, which three more keys would have cost. A window is a promise about what was analysed and a shorter one is not free: every attack and crest reading here is taken over it, and the difference between 44 and 60 ms is most of a closed hat.
_groups: Twelve of the kit's thirteen, and every one of them whole, which is the point of this gate. `guiro` is the exception and carries no group: the short guiro records 45 ms and cannot fill the window, and a family of one holds no relation.
_velocities: One, and 100 is a label rather than a measurement: the font sets `velRange` on no zone, so it holds one recording per note at a velocity it does not state.
_stimulus: Nothing played this. The recordings are read out of the source, so there is no preroll to strip, no settle to wait out and no warmup to play in.
_dry: Nothing played this, so nothing was switched off. What the file holds is the module's own PCM with no effect in front of it, which the importer re-measures rather than trusts.
_note_map: There is deliberately none. This source IS the GS kit map, so its keys are GM's by construction.
_dimensions: Three, and the cut is the gate's rather than a judgement about what matters. Sixty milliseconds is the strike and not the sound after it: a decay rate read over it is the attack transient wearing a decay's name, and a ring has not begun. What sixty milliseconds does hold is how hard each piece hits, how peaked that hit is, and how loud it is against every other piece - which is the reading this grid exists for.

dimensions_na.band_decay: the window is 60 ms and a band decay read over it measures the attack transient rather than the damping. `drums_module` reads it for the pieces that ring past 400 ms and `drums_module_mid` for the ones that stop between.
dimensions_na.ring: as `band_decay`: at 60 ms the ring has not begun.
dimensions_na.vel_range: the font declares no velocity layers at all - `velRange` is set on none of its zones, so it holds one recording per note at a velocity it does not state.
dimensions_na.band_tilt: colour, which `policy.json` assigns to the modern reference for a kit and not to the module. `drums.json` gates it.
dimensions_na.stereo: the recordings are single-channel, so a width is zero by construction rather than by voicing.

_identity: Which file and which of its presets answered this timbre lives in the untracked sibling `drums_module_hit.local.json`.
_timbres: `channel` is what makes a note number select an instrument rather than a pitch, and it is what `profile.py` reads to choose the percussion metric set over the pitched one.
